# 8098 - TRI-STATE hex inverter (inverting buffer)

Package DIP-16 · family 8000 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/8098.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/8098.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 48 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![8098 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/8098.png) | ![8098 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/block-8098.png) | ![8098 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/block-8098.png) |

A rectangle for the whole function (or one section of it). Pin numbers are written on the lines where they meet the box; signal names are written beside them.

How to tell it on a drawing: Read the part type from the parts list and compare the pin numbers against this cut-out.

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

## Pins

| Pin | Name | Role | Active | Output type | Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | G1 | enable | low |  | controls pins 3, 5, 7, 9; when not enabled: float |
| 2 | A1 | input |  |  |  |
| 3 | Y1 | output |  | three-state | enabled by G1 |
| 4 | A2 | input |  |  |  |
| 5 | Y2 | output |  | three-state | enabled by G1 |
| 6 | A3 | input |  |  |  |
| 7 | Y3 | output |  | three-state | enabled by G1 |
| 8 | GND | ground |  |  |  |
| 9 | Y4 | output |  | three-state | enabled by G1 |
| 10 | A4 | input |  |  |  |
| 11 | Y5 | output |  | three-state | enabled by G2 |
| 12 | A5 | input |  |  |  |
| 13 | Y6 | output |  | three-state | enabled by G2 |
| 14 | A6 | input |  |  |  |
| 15 | G2 | enable | low |  | controls pins 11, 13; when not enabled: float |
| 16 | VCC | power |  |  | +5 V |

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 3,5,7,9 | Yn = An' when G1' ; Z when G1 high | Y1..Y4 give the inverse of A1..A4 while G1 is low; they float (high impedance) while G1 is high. |
| 11,13 | Yn = An' when G2' ; Z when G2 high | Y5, Y6 give the inverse of A5, A6 while G2 is low; they float while G2 is high. |

| G | Y | PZH | 21 | 35 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 50 pF, RL 400 ohm |
| G | Y | PZL | 24 | 37 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 50 pF, RL 400 ohm |
| G | Y | PHZ | 6 | 11 | VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 5 pF, RL 400 ohm |

## Not known

- No minimum propagation delays are printed (path-delay function uses 0 ns).
- Switching table text layer is partly garbled; values were read in column order (DM70/80 95,97 and 96,98 columns).
- Which buffers G1 and G2 control was read from the high-resolution 8097 diagram; the 8098 diagram was only seen at page resolution, drawn the same way.

## Notes

Four buffers on G1, two on G2. Datasheet says pin equivalent to DM54368.

- [National Semiconductor 1976 TTL Databook, DM70/DM8095,L95,96,L96,97,L97,98,L98 TRI-STATE Hex Buffers](https://www.bitsavers.org/components/national/_dataBooks/1976_National_TTL_Databook.pdf) - pdf 352-353 (printed 3-7, 3-8); DM8098
